qualification: local pinned-fixture A05.3 dispatcher-entry measurement; not hardware, cross-host, G1-G5, or release qualification

gate.requirement: dispatcher entries per 1M instructions fall by more than 95 percent on kernel boot

interpretation: The implementation is exercised in production and remains correct through cache rotations, but it does not satisfy the A05.3 dispatcher gate. Fault-capable and restartable-memory blocks deliberately cannot become raw generated-chain targets because the current executor owns only one Swift checkpoint per entry. A05.4 instruction-boundary metadata and deoptimization are required before those dominant kernel paths can chain safely.

verification.dbtPCAndRunnerGate: 1,529 tests in 178 suites passed; the environment-driven pinned boot test skipped because its variables were absent, then this runner executed the same pinned inputs explicitly.
verification.protectedChainRegression: Stable protected-memory execution avoids reachable-graph byte validation; a checked code mutation advances the global generation, unlinks raw targets, and recompiles changed bytes.
verification.postFixHostSample: The earlier O(graph) validateDirectChainTargets hotspot is absent; execution is dominated by normal native execution and translation misses.

limitations: The successful workload evidence contains one candidate run on one local Apple M2 Pro.
The within-run baseline is nativeDispatcherEntries plus generated bypasses; the prior-frozen comparison uses translated block entries normalized by baseline-JIT instructions.
IBTC and shadow-return hit rates remain negligible because most resolved targets are not yet safe restart boundaries.
The greater-than-95-percent gate failed and A05.3 remains open.
